##### `with` <a name="with" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.with"></a>

```typescript
public with(mixins: ...IMixin[]): IConstruct
```

Applies one or more mixins to this construct.

Mixins are applied in order. The list of constructs is captured at the
start of the call, so constructs added by a mixin will not be visited.
Use multiple `with()` calls if subsequent mixins should apply to added
constructs.

##### `applyCrossStackReferenceStrength` <a name="applyCrossStackReferenceStrength" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.applyCrossStackReferenceStrength"></a>

```typescript
public applyCrossStackReferenceStrength(strength: ReferenceStrength): void
```

Override the cross-stack reference strength for this resource.

When set, any cross-stack reference to this resource will use the specified
mechanism instead of the global default determined by the
`@aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackReferences` context key. This is useful for
selectively weakening specific references to avoid the "deadly embrace" problem
without changing the app-wide default.

###### `strength`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="strength" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.applyCrossStackReferenceStrength.parameter.strength"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.ReferenceStrength

The reference strength to use for this resource.

---

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy: RemovalPolicy): void
```

Apply the given removal policy to this resource.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`).

###### `policy`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.Action.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Action.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.Action.isOwnedResource(construct: IConstruct)
```

### Alert <a name="Alert" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.Alert"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.IAlert

A PostHog logs alert: counts log entries matching a filter over a time window and fires when the count crosses a threshold.

Notification
destinations are managed separately.

#### Initializers <a name="Initializers" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.Alert.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { logs } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

new logs.Alert(scope: Construct, id: string, props: AlertProps)
```

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.Alert.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { logs } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

logs.Alert.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.Alert.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

Override the cross-stack reference strength for this resource.

When set, any cross-stack reference to this resource will use the specified
mechanism instead of the global default determined by the
`@aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackReferences` context key. This is useful for
selectively weakening specific references to avoid the "deadly embrace" problem
without changing the app-wide default.

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Annotation.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy: RemovalPolicy): void
```

Apply the given removal policy to this resource.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`).

###### `policy`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Annotation.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Annotation.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.Annotation.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Annotation.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### ApprovalPolicy <a name="ApprovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.ApprovalPolicy"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.IApprovalPolicy

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.AssignmentRule.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.AssignmentRule.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

Any object.

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAction.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAction.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAction.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

###### `policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.CfnAlert.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.CfnAlert.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAlert.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { logs } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

logs.CfnAlert.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { logs } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

logs.CfnAlert.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.CfnAlert.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlert.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any


##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

---

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

###### `policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAnnotation.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

---


##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { projects } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { projects } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

projects.CfnApprovalPolicy.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

---

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnAssignmentRule.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

---

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { batchExports } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { batchExports } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.batchExports.CfnBatchExport.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

---

and the dependency will automatically be transferred to the relevant scope.

##### `applyRemovalPolicy` <a name="applyRemovalPolicy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.applyRemovalPolicy"></a>

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

###### `policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnCohort.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboard.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDashboardTemplate.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.CfnDataColorTheme.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.CfnDomain.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.CfnDomain.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.CfnDomain.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.CfnDomain.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { organizations } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

organizations.CfnDomain.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.CfnDomain.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { organizations } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

organizations.CfnDomain.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

###### `policy`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="policy" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.applyRemovalPolicy.parameter.policy"></a>

- *Type:* aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { featureFlags } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isCfnElement` <a name="isCfnElement" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isCfnElement"></a>

```typescript
import { featureFlags } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnEarlyAccessFeature.isCfnElement.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.CfnEndpoint.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.CfnEndpoint.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.CfnEndpoint.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy?: RemovalPolicy, options?: RemovalPolicyOptions): void
```

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)
