##### `addOverride` <a name="addOverride" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnWebExperiment.addOverride"></a>

```typescript
public addOverride(path: string, value: any): void
```

Adds an override to the synthesized CloudFormation resource.

To add a
property override, either use `addPropertyOverride` or prefix `path` with
"Properties." (i.e. `Properties.TopicName`).

If the override is nested, separate each nested level using a dot (.) in the path parameter.
If there is an array as part of the nesting, specify the index in the path.

To include a literal `.` in the property name, prefix with a `\`. In most
programming languages you will need to write this as `"\\."` because the
`\` itself will need to be escaped.

For example,
```typescript
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.0.Projection.NonKeyAttributes', ['myattribute']);
cfnResource.addOverride('Properties.GlobalSecondaryIndexes.1.ProjectionType', 'INCLUDE');
```
would add the overrides
```json
"Properties": {
  "GlobalSecondaryIndexes": [
    {
      "Projection": {
        "NonKeyAttributes": [ "myattribute" ]
        ...
      }
      ...
    },
    {
      "ProjectionType": "INCLUDE"
      ...
    },
  ]
  ...
}
```

The `value` argument to `addOverride` will not be processed or translated
in any way. Pass raw JSON values in here with the correct capitalization
for CloudFormation. If you pass CDK classes or structs, they will be
rendered with lowercased key names, and CloudFormation will reject the
template.

###### `path`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="path" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnWebExperiment.addOverride.parameter.path"></a>

- *Type:* string

The path of the property, you can use dot notation to override values in complex types.

Any intermediate keys
will be created as needed.

---

###### `value`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="value" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnWebExperiment.addOverride.parameter.value"></a>

- *Type:* any

The value.

Could be primitive or complex.

Sets the deletion policy of the resource based on the removal policy specified.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`). In some
cases, a snapshot can be taken of the resource prior to deletion
(`RemovalPolicy.SNAPSHOT`). A list of resources that support this policy
can be found in the following link:

> [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html#aws-attribute-deletionpolicy-options)

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnWebExperiment.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { experiments } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

experiments.CfnWebExperiment.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnWebExperiment.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { experiments } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

experiments.CfnWebExperiment.isCfnElement(x: any)
```

Returns `true` if a construct is a stack element (i.e. part of the synthesized cloudformation template).

Uses duck-typing instead of `instanceof` to allow stack elements from different
versions of this library to be included in the same stack.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Cohort.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.Cohort.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Cohort.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.DashboardBase.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.DashboardBase.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.DashboardBase.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---


##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.DataColorTheme.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.DataColorTheme.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.DataColorTheme.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.EarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { featureFlags } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

featureFlags.EarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.EarlyAccessFeature.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.


##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.Evaluation.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { llmAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

llmAnalytics.Evaluation.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.Evaluation.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### EventDefinition <a name="EventDefinition" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.EventDefinition"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.IEventDefinition

A PostHog event definition: the metadata PostHog keeps for an event name (description, owner, tags, verification, visibility and schema enforcement).

Requires a PostHog plan with data management.

PostHog creates an event definition automatically the first time it
ingests an event. Creating a definition for an event that has already been
ingested fails with `AlreadyExists`: import such events into the stack
(`cdk import`, with the project ID and the definition's PostHog ID) instead
of creating them. Use this construct to create definitions for events that
haven't been sent yet.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.EventDefinition.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.EventDefinition.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.EventDefinition.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### Experiment <a name="Experiment" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.Experiment"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.IExperiment

A PostHog experiment (A/B test): a feature flag with variants plus the metrics used to compare them.

Deleting it soft-deletes the experiment; the feature flag stays.

### FeatureExperiment <a name="FeatureExperiment" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.FeatureExperiment"></a>

An A/B test set up end to end from one definition: a multivariate feature flag with the variants and targeting, the experiment linked to it, a results dashboard and, optionally, an early access feature.

The experiment is linked by key to the flag this construct creates, and
depends on it, so PostHog never creates a second flag. The flag stays the
source of truth for variants and targeting; PostHog reads the variants
from it.

Each dashboard insight is derived from its metric and broken down by the
`$feature/<flagKey>` event property: mean metrics become a trends insight
of the metric's source, funnel metrics a funnel from the exposure event
through the metric's steps, ratio metrics a trends insight with the
formula `A / B`. Metrics the pattern can't map (e.g. from
`ExperimentMetric.fromJson()`) fall back to exposure events per variant.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.FeatureExperiment.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { patterns } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

patterns.FeatureExperiment.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.FeatureExperiment.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

without a lookup at deploy time. So `flagId` throws when read: the
imported flag can be referenced by key (e.g. in SDK config or
experiments that take a key), but can't be linked to an early access
feature or a scheduled change. Use `fromFlagId()` or

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.GroupingRule.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.GroupingRule.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.GroupingRule.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.


##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.HogFunction.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { cdp } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

cdp.HogFunction.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.HogFunction.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---


##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Insight.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { productAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

productAnalytics.Insight.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.Insight.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript

productAnalytics.InsightVariable.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.InsightVariable.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.MessageTemplate.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { workflows } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

workflows.MessageTemplate.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.MessageTemplate.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.sessionReplay.Playlist.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { sessionReplay } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

sessionReplay.Playlist.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.sessionReplay.Playlist.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.


### PostHogProject <a name="PostHogProject" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogProject"></a>

A production-ready PostHog project: the project with internal and test traffic filtered out, and optionally a managed reverse proxy, a verified organization domain, a secret API key, stack outputs and SSM parameters that applications read their PostHog settings from.

The project is retained when it is removed from the stack (deleting it
deletes all its data), unless `removalPolicy` says otherwise.

### PostHogResourceTypeRegistration <a name="PostHogResourceTypeRegistration" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypeRegistration"></a>

Registers one PostHog resource type privately in this account and region: uploads its handler package, creates its execution role, registers a version (`AWS::CloudFormation::ResourceVersion`), makes it the default version and sets its type configuration (API key and base URL).

Usually created by `PostHogResourceTypes`.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypeRegistration.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { patterns } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

patterns.PostHogResourceTypeRegistration.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypeRegistration.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### PostHogResourceTypes <a name="PostHogResourceTypes" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypes"></a>

Registers the PostHog CloudFormation resource types (`PostHog::*`) privately in the deploying account and region, replacing `cfn submit` and `aws cloudformation set-type-configuration`.

For each type it uploads the handler package, creates the execution role,
a log group and logging role, registers a version, makes it the default and
sets the type configuration through a custom resource. The API key is
passed as a Secrets Manager dynamic reference
(`{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}`) that CloudFormation resolves each time
it runs a handler, so the key never appears in the template or the type
configuration.

**Consumers must deploy after this construct.** CloudFormation only knows a
`PostHog::*` type once it is registered, so any construct (or whole stack)
that uses PostHog resources must depend on it: call
`registration.addDependent(constructOrStack)`, or add a dependency on
`registration.ready`. Ideally keep this construct in its own stack.

Handler packages must exist at synth time (`make package` at the
repository root). First-time registration takes several minutes per type.

#### Initializers <a name="Initializers" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypes.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { patterns } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

new patterns.PostHogResourceTypes(scope: Construct, id: string, props: PostHogResourceTypesProps)
```

| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.PostHogResourceTypes.Initializer.parameter.scope">scope</a></code> | <code>constructs.Construct</code> | *No description.* |

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.surveys.ProductTour.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { surveys } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

surveys.ProductTour.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.surveys.ProductTour.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### Project <a name="Project" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.Project"></a>

A PostHog project and its main settings.

Settings left out are not managed: PostHog keeps whatever is set in the UI.
Removing a setting that was managed resets it to PostHog's default.

Use `Project.fromProjectId()` to reference an existing project.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.Project.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { organizations } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

organizations.Project.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.Project.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---


Override the cross-stack reference strength for this resource.

When set, any cross-stack reference to this resource will use the specified
mechanism instead of the global default determined by the
`@aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackReferences` context key. This is useful for
selectively weakening specific references to avoid the "deadly embrace" problem
without changing the app-wide default.

Apply the given removal policy to this resource.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`).

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.ProjectBase.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { organizations } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

organizations.ProjectBase.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.ProjectBase.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

```typescript
import { organizations } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

organizations.ProjectBase.isOwnedResource(construct: IConstruct)
```

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.ProviderKey.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { llmAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

llmAnalytics.ProviderKey.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.ProviderKey.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

### ProxyRecord <a name="ProxyRecord" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.ProxyRecord"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.organizations.IProxyRecord

A PostHog managed reverse proxy: a subdomain you own through which SDKs send data to PostHog.

After the CNAME record exists, PostHog verifies it
and issues a certificate; `status` moves from `waiting` through `issuing`

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.RetentionRule.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { logs } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

logs.RetentionRule.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.RetentionRule.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

### S3BatchExport <a name="S3BatchExport" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.patterns.S3BatchExport"></a>

A PostHog batch export to S3, with the AWS side wired up: the bucket, a least-privilege IAM user, its access key in a Secrets Manager secret, and optionally a data warehouse table that reads the files back.

Nobody copies credentials by hand. The batch export receives the access
key only as `{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}` dynamic references to the
secret, which CloudFormation resolves at deploy time, so the secret access
key never appears in the PostHog resource's properties. The secret itself
is created from the `AWS::IAM::AccessKey`'s `SecretAccessKey` attribute
(the standard CDK pattern): the key never appears in plain text in the
template, but anyone who can read the stack's resources through
CloudFormation or read the secret can obtain it.

Permissions of the writer user: `s3:PutObject` (which also authorizes
`CreateMultipartUpload`, `UploadPart` and `CompleteMultipartUpload`),
`s3:AbortMultipartUpload` and `s3:ListMultipartUploadParts` on
`bucket/prefix*`. PostHog's S3 export only writes; it does not list or
read the bucket, so `s3:ListBucket` and `s3:GetObject` are not granted.
With a KMS key it also gets `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:Encrypt` and
`kms:Decrypt` (S3 needs `kms:Decrypt` to complete multipart uploads).

With `readBack`, a second user with `s3:GetObject` on `bucket/prefix*`
and `s3:ListBucket` restricted to the prefix (plus `kms:Decrypt`) gets its
own access key and secret for the table.

**Key rotation:** increase `keySerial` and deploy. That creates new
access keys, stores them in new secrets and updates the batch export (and
table) to reference them; CloudFormation deletes the old keys and secrets
when the update completes. Updating the existing secret in place would not
work: the dynamic references in the PostHog resources would be unchanged,
so CloudFormation would not send the new credentials to PostHog.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.SavedMetric.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { experiments } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

experiments.SavedMetric.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.SavedMetric.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.ScheduledChange.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { featureFlags } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

featureFlags.ScheduledChange.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.SchemaPropertyGroup.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript

productAnalytics.SchemaPropertyGroup.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.SchemaPropertyGroup.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

### SecretApiKey <a name="SecretApiKey" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.SecretApiKey"></a>

- *Implements:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.ISecretApiKey

A PostHog project secret API key (`phs_...`): a project-scoped key with a fixed set of API scopes, for server-side use such as local feature flag evaluation.

The key value never appears in the template: PostHog returns it once and
the resource type writes it to a Secrets Manager secret. Read it from
`secret`, e.g. with `grantRead()` and `ecs.Secret.fromSecretsManager()`.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.Source.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { dataWarehouse } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

dataWarehouse.Source.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.Source.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.SuppressionRule.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

errorTracking.SuppressionRule.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.SuppressionRule.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---


Override the cross-stack reference strength for this resource.

When set, any cross-stack reference to this resource will use the specified
mechanism instead of the global default determined by the
`@aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackReferences` context key. This is useful for
selectively weakening specific references to avoid the "deadly embrace" problem
without changing the app-wide default.

```typescript
public applyRemovalPolicy(policy: RemovalPolicy): void
```

Apply the given removal policy to this resource.

The Removal Policy controls what happens to this resource when it stops
being managed by CloudFormation, either because you've removed it from the
CDK application or because you've made a change that requires the resource
to be replaced.

The resource can be deleted (`RemovalPolicy.DESTROY`), or left in your AWS
account for data recovery and cleanup later (`RemovalPolicy.RETAIN`).

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.Table.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { dataWarehouse } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

dataWarehouse.Table.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.dataWarehouse.Table.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

- *Type:* any

Any object.

---

##### `isConstruct` <a name="isConstruct" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.WebExperiment.isConstruct"></a>

```typescript
import { experiments } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

experiments.WebExperiment.isConstruct(x: any)
```

Checks if `x` is a construct.

Use this method instead of `instanceof` to properly detect `Construct`
instances, even when the construct library is symlinked.

Explanation: in JavaScript, multiple copies of the `constructs` library on
disk are seen as independent, completely different libraries. As a
consequence, the class `Construct` in each copy of the `constructs` library
is seen as a different class, and an instance of one class will not test as
`instanceof` the other class. `npm install` will not create installations
like this, but users may manually symlink construct libraries together or
use a monorepo tool: in those cases, multiple copies of the `constructs`
library can be accidentally installed, and `instanceof` will behave
unpredictably. It is safest to avoid using `instanceof`, and using
this type-testing method instead.

###### `x`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="x" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.WebExperiment.isConstruct.parameter.x"></a>

Any object.

### ActionStep <a name="ActionStep" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.ActionStep"></a>

An event matches the action when it

must match.

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'
```

| --- | --- | --- |

### AlertOptions <a name="AlertOptions" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions"></a>

Options for creating a logs alert in a project.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
const alertOptions: logs.AlertOptions = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Name of the alert. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.annotations">annotations</a></code> | <code>{[ key: string ]: string}</code> | Context for responders, e.g. `{ runbook_url: 'https://...' }`. Only alerts evaluated by the PostHog alerts platform can have annotations. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.blockedWindows">blockedWindows</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.BlockedWindow[]</code> | Quiet hours: up to five local time windows (project timezone) when the alert does not run. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.cooldown">cooldown</a></code> | <code>aws-cdk-lib.Duration</code> | Minimum time between notifications, in whole minutes. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.datapointsToAlarm">datapointsToAlarm</a></code> | <code>number</code> | Number of periods within the evaluation window that must breach the threshold to fire (N in N-of-M), 1 to `evaluationPeriods`. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.enabled">enabled</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the alert is evaluated. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.evaluationPeriods">evaluationPeriods</a></code> | <code>number</code> | Number of check periods in the sliding evaluation window (M in N-of-M), 1 to 10. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.filters">filters</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.LogFilter</code> | Further conditions log entries must match. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.labels">labels</a></code> | <code>{[ key: string ]: string}</code> | Labels saying who owns the alert and how urgent it is, e.g. `{ team: 'checkout' }`. `alertname` and names starting with `posthog_` are reserved. Only alerts evaluated by the PostHog alerts platform can have labels. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.removalPolicy">removalPolicy</a></code> | <code>aws-cdk-lib.RemovalPolicy</code> | What happens to the PostHog alert when it is removed from the stack. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.serviceNames">serviceNames</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Service names to count. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.AlertOptions.property.severityLevels">severityLevels</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.logs.LogSeverity[]</code> | Severity levels to count. |

| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.ApprovalPolicyOptions.property.actionKey">actionKey</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Key of the gated action, e.g. `feature_flag.update`. 1 to 128 characters. |

| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.ApprovalPolicyOptions.property.rawApproverConfig">rawApproverConfig</a></code> | <code>{[ key: string ]: any}</code> | Escape hatch: PostHog's `approver_config` JSON object as-is, e.g. `{ users: [1, 2], roles: [], quorum: 1 }`. Use it when the typed `approverConfig` does not cover a field PostHog accepts. |

Notification destinations are managed separately.

### CfnAlertProps <a name="CfnAlertProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.productAnalytics.CfnAlertProps"></a>

A PostHog insight alert: checks an insight's value on a schedule against a threshold (or an anomaly detector) and notifies subscribed users when it fires.

Runtime state (state, last checked/notified, check history) is not part of the resource.

A PostHog annotation: a note pinned to a point in time (a release, incident or campaign) and shown on insight charts in a project, an organization, a dashboard or a single insight.

### CfnApprovalPolicyProps <a name="CfnApprovalPolicyProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps"></a>

A PostHog approval policy: requires changes of one kind (the action key, e.g. changes to feature flags) in a project to be approved by designated approvers before they are applied.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript

const cfnApprovalPolicyProps: projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.actionKey">actionKey</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Key of the gated action, e.g. feature_flag.update. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.approverConfig">approverConfig</a></code> | <code>string</code> | JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString) describing who can approve and how many approvals are needed, e.g. {"users": [1, 2], "roles": [], "quorum": 1}. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the approval policy belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.allowSelfApprove">allowSelfApprove</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the requester of a change may approve it. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.bypassOrgMembershipLevels">bypassOrgMembershipLevels</a></code> | <code>string</code> | JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString) of organization membership levels whose members can apply the change without approval. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.bypassRoles">bypassRoles</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | IDs (UUIDs) of roles whose members can apply the change without approval. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.conditions">conditions</a></code> | <code>string</code> | JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString) restricting which changes of the action need approval. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.enabled">enabled</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the policy is enforced. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.projects.CfnApprovalPolicyProps.property.expiresAfter">expiresAfter</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Auto-expire pending change requests after this duration, as a Django duration string such as "7 00:00:00" (7 days) or "12:00:00" (12 hours), or ISO 8601 such as P7D. |

### CfnEvaluationProps <a name="CfnEvaluationProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps"></a>

A PostHog LLM analytics evaluation: scores LLM generations, traces or sessions with an LLM judge, Hog code or sentiment classification.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { llmAnalytics } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

const cfnEvaluationProps: llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.evaluationType">evaluationType</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationPropsEvaluationType</code> | `llm_judge` scores outputs with an LLM against a prompt; |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Name of the evaluation. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.outputType">outputType</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationPropsOutputType</code> | Output format: `boolean` (pass/fail), `numeric` (finite score), `categorical` (category keys) or `sentiment`. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the evaluation belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.conditions">conditions</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Trigger conditions as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString). |

| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.directoryId">directoryId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the directory (folder) containing the evaluation. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.enabled">enabled</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the evaluation runs automatically on new $ai_generation events. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.evaluationConfig">evaluationConfig</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Evaluation configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.modelConfiguration">modelConfiguration</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationModelConfiguration</code> | Provider and model of the LLM judge. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.outputConfig">outputConfig</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Output configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.target">target</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationPropsTarget</code> | What the evaluation runs on: `generation` (default, each matching $ai_generation event), `trace` (the whole trace once) or `session` (the whole $ai_session_id session once). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.targetConfig">targetConfig</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Settle configuration for `trace` and `session` targets as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): {"strategy": "fixed_window", "window_seconds": N} or {"strategy": "inactivity", "quiet_period_seconds": N, "max_age_seconds": N}. |

```typescript

```

- *Default:* false.

Whether the evaluation runs automatically on new $ai_generation events.


- *Type:* string

Evaluation configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString).

For `llm_judge`: {"prompt": "..."} plus optional `judge_method` (`llm` or `decision`), `include_media` and `reasoning_level`; for `hog`: {"source": "<Hog code>"}; for `sentiment`: {"source": "user_messages"}.


Provider and model of the LLM judge.

Required for `llm_judge` evaluations; leave it out for `hog` and `sentiment`.

```typescript
public readonly outputConfig: string;
```

- *Type:* string

Output configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString).

Boolean: `allows_na`, `true_is_failure`, `decision_threshold`; numeric: `min`, `max`, `step`, `passing_rule` ({operator: gte|lte, threshold}); categorical: `options` ([{key, label}]), `selection_mode` (single|multiple), `passing_rule` ({categories}).

---

##### `target`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="target" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.target"></a>

```typescript

```

What the evaluation runs on: `generation` (default, each matching $ai_generation event), `trace` (the whole trace once) or `session` (the whole $ai_session_id session once).

---

##### `targetConfig`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="targetConfig" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.llmAnalytics.CfnEvaluationProps.property.targetConfig"></a>

```typescript
public readonly targetConfig: string;
```

- *Type:* string

Settle configuration for `trace` and `session` targets as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): {"strategy": "fixed_window", "window_seconds": N} or {"strategy": "inactivity", "quiet_period_seconds": N, "max_age_seconds": N}.

Omit for `generation`; PostHog fills in omitted fields with per-target defaults.

### CfnFeatureFlagProps <a name="CfnFeatureFlagProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps"></a>

A PostHog feature flag: a key that SDKs evaluate to roll features out to a percentage of users, to specific users or groups, or to serve multivariate variants and payloads.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { featureFlags } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

const cfnFeatureFlagProps: featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.key">key</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Feature flag key that SDKs evaluate, e.g. new-checkout. Must be unique within the project. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the feature flag belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.active">active</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the feature flag is enabled. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.archived">archived</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the flag is archived. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.bucketingIdentifier">bucketingIdentifier</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagPropsBucketingIdentifier</code> | Identifier used to bucket users into rollout percentages and variants: `distinct_id` (the default) or `device_id`. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.ensureExperienceContinuity">ensureExperienceContinuity</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to persist a user's flag value across the anonymous-to-identified transition. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.evaluationContexts">evaluationContexts</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Evaluation contexts that control where the flag evaluates at runtime. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.evaluationRuntime">evaluationRuntime</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagPropsEvaluationRuntime</code> | Where the flag is allowed to evaluate: `server` (server-side SDKs only), `client` (client-side SDKs only) or `all` (both, the default). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.filters">filters</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Targeting configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): `groups` (release condition groups with `properties`, `rollout_percentage` and optional `variant`), `multivariate` (`variants` with `key` and `rollout_percentage`), `payloads` (payload values keyed by variant key, or `true` for boolean flags), `aggregation_group_type_index` and `early_exit`. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.isRemoteConfiguration">isRemoteConfiguration</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether this flag is a remote configuration flag that delivers a payload rather than gating a feature. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Description of the feature flag (PostHog stores it in the `name` field for backwards compatibility). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.tags">tags</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Organizational tags for the feature flag. |

---


- *Default:* true.

Defaults to true.

```typescript

```

Identifier used to bucket users into rollout percentages and variants: `distinct_id` (the default) or `device_id`.


Incompatible with device_id bucketing.

```typescript
public readonly evaluationContexts: string[];
```

- *Type:* string[]

Evaluation contexts that control where the flag evaluates at runtime.

PostHog does not return this field, so it is write-only.

---

##### `evaluationRuntime`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="evaluationRuntime" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.evaluationRuntime"></a>

```typescript
public readonly evaluationRuntime: CfnFeatureFlagPropsEvaluationRuntime;
```

- *Type:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagPropsEvaluationRuntime

Where the flag is allowed to evaluate: `server` (server-side SDKs only), `client` (client-side SDKs only) or `all` (both, the default).

---

##### `filters`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="filters" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.featureFlags.CfnFeatureFlagProps.property.filters"></a>

```typescript
public readonly filters: string;
```

- *Type:* string

Targeting configuration as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): `groups` (release condition groups with `properties`, `rollout_percentage` and optional `variant`), `multivariate` (`variants` with `key` and `rollout_percentage`), `payloads` (payload values keyed by variant key, or `true` for boolean flags), `aggregation_group_type_index` and `early_exit`.

Leave unset for a flag with no release conditions.

---

```typescript
public readonly isRemoteConfiguration: boolean;
```

- *Type:* boolean

Whether this flag is a remote configuration flag that delivers a payload rather than gating a feature.

```typescript
public readonly name: string;
```

- *Type:* string

Description of the feature flag (PostHog stores it in the `name` field for backwards compatibility).

### CfnGroupingRuleProps <a name="CfnGroupingRuleProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnGroupingRuleProps"></a>

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnGroupingRuleProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { errorTracking } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

```

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.errorTracking.CfnGroupingRuleProps.property.filters">filters</a></code> | <code>string</code> | JSON (use Fn::ToJsonString). |

### CfnHogFlowProps <a name="CfnHogFlowProps" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps"></a>

A PostHog workflow (hog flow): a trigger followed by a graph of actions (messages, delays, branches) that PostHog runs for each person who enters it.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { workflows } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

const cfnHogFlowProps: workflows.CfnHogFlowProps = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.actions">actions</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Ordered action nodes as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString): [{"id", "name", "type", "config", "description"?, "on_error"?, "filters"?, "output_variable"?}]. Exactly one action with type `trigger` is required (its config defines the workflow trigger), and typically one `exit`. Types: trigger, function, function_email, function_sms, function_push, delay, wait_until_condition, wait_until_time_window, conditional_branch, random_cohort_branch, exit, email_sandbox. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Workflow name. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the workflow belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.conversion">conversion</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Conversion goal as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): {"filters": [property filters], "events": [{"filters": {"events": [...]}}], "window": "7d"}. Required for the exit_on_conversion exit conditions. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.description">description</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Optional description. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.edges">edges</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Graph edges as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString): [{"from", "to", "type": "continue"\|"branch", "index"?}]. `branch` requires `index` (into config.conditions of a conditional_branch or wait_until_condition). Every non-exit action needs a reachable next action. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.emailSendingRateLimit">emailSendingRateLimit</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowEmailSendingRateLimit</code> | Optional email pacing for deliverability. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.exitCondition">exitCondition</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowPropsExitCondition</code> | When people leave the workflow early. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.originProduct">originProduct</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowPropsOriginProduct</code> | Product surface that owns this workflow, e.g. `loops`. Can only be set on create. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.status">status</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowPropsStatus</code> | `draft` (no execution, the PostHog default), `active` (live) or `archived` (disabled). |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.tags">tags</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Tags for organizing workflows, for example by team or use case. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.triggerMasking">triggerMasking</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowTriggerMasking</code> | Optional dedup/throttle on an already-matched trigger. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnHogFlowProps.property.variables">variables</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Workflow variables as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString): [{"key", "type": "string"\|"number"\|"boolean", "default"}]. |

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.Initializer"></a>


| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Display name for the function. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the function belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.type">type</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionPropsType</code> | Function type. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.description">description</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Human-readable description of what this function does. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.enabled">enabled</a></code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the function is active and processing events. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.executionOrder">executionOrder</a></code> | <code>number</code> | Execution priority for transformations. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.filters">filters</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Event filters that control which events trigger the function, as a JSON object (use Fn::ToJsonString): {"events": [...], "actions": [...], "properties": [...], "filter_test_accounts": bool, "source": "events"}. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.hog">hog</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Source code: Hog for most types, TypeScript for site_destination and site_app. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.iconUrl">iconUrl</a></code> | <code>string</code> | URL of the icon displayed in the PostHog UI. |

Wrap each value in {"value": ...}. Inputs that the schema marks secret go in SecretInputs instead. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.inputsSchema">inputsSchema</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Schema of the function's configurable inputs as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString): [{"key", "type", "label"?, "required"?, "secret"?, "default"?, ...}]. When TemplateId is set and this is omitted, the template's schema is used. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.mappings">mappings</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Event-to-destination mappings as a JSON array (use Fn::ToJsonString): [{"name", "filters", "inputs", "inputs_schema"}]. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.masking">masking</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionMasking</code> | PII masking: suppress repeat events with the same hash within the TTL. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.secretInputs">secretInputs</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Values of the secret inputs (API tokens, passwords), as a JSON object in the same shape as Inputs (use Fn::ToJsonString with a dynamic reference, e.g. {"api_key": {"value": "{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}"}}). Each key must be marked "secret": true in the inputs schema. Write-only: never returned by Read. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.cdp.CfnHogFunctionProps.property.templateId">templateId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the template to create this function from, e.g. template-slack or template-webhook. PostHog copies the template's code, inputs schema and defaults. Can only be set on create. |

```typescript
import { experiments } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

const cfnHoldoutProps: experiments.CfnHoldoutProps = { ... }
```

| --- | --- | --- |

| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnHoldoutProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Human-readable name of the holdout group. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.experiments.CfnHoldoutProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the holdout belongs to. |

```typescript

```

- *Type:* string

Non-empty JSON array of release condition groups defining the held-out population (use Fn::ToJsonString), in the same shape as feature flag release conditions.

Each group's `rollout_percentage` (0-100) is the share of users held back; `properties` optionally narrows the group. Don't set `variant`: PostHog sets it to holdout-<id>. Only the first group's rollout_percentage is embedded in linked experiments' flags.

A PostHog messaging category: a named group of workflow messages (marketing or transactional) that recipients can opt out of on the preferences page.

#### Initializer <a name="Initializer" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.Initializer"></a>

```typescript
import { workflows } from '@posthog/cdk-constructs'

const cfnMessageCategoryProps: workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps = { ... }
```

#### Properties <a name="Properties" id="Properties"></a>

| **Name** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.key">key</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Stable identifier for the category, unique within the project, for example `newsletter`. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.name">name</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Display name of the category, shown in the PostHog app. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.projectId">projectId</a></code> | <code>string</code> | ID of the PostHog project the message category belongs to. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.categoryType">categoryType</a></code> | <code>@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryPropsCategoryType</code> | `marketing` (the PostHog default): recipients can opt out of it, and sends skip recipients who did. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.description">description</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Internal notes about which messages belong to this category. |
| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.publicDescription">publicDescription</a></code> | <code>string</code> | Description that recipients see next to the category on the preferences page. |

---

##### `key`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="key" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.key"></a>

```typescript

```

Opt-out lists and preference imports refer to categories by key. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `name`<sup>Required</sup> <a name="name" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.name"></a>

```typescript
public readonly name: string;
```

- *Type:* string

Display name of the category, shown in the PostHog app.

```typescript
public readonly projectId: string;
```

- *Type:* string

ID of the PostHog project the message category belongs to.

---

##### `categoryType`<sup>Optional</sup> <a name="categoryType" id="@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryProps.property.categoryType"></a>

```typescript
public readonly categoryType: CfnMessageCategoryPropsCategoryType;
```

- *Type:* @posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageCategoryPropsCategoryType

`marketing` (the PostHog default): recipients can opt out of it, and sends skip recipients who did.

`transactional`: for messages a recipient must get, such as receipts or password resets; sends ignore opt-outs and the category doesn't appear on the preferences page.

A PostHog messaging template: reusable email content (subject, body, sender) that workflow email steps and the transactional email API send.

Replaced as a whole on update. |

| <code><a href="#@posthog/cdk-constructs.workflows.CfnMessageTemplateProps.property.tags">tags</a></code> | <code>string[]</code> | Tags for organizing templates, for example by team or use case. |
